distance_ridge — 3D medial op

• Data kinds: voxel → voxel

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.distance_ridge(vol, min_radius=0.0) (to call the implementation directly, import medial; medial.distance_ridge(vol, min_radius=0.0); from the registry, ops3d.get("distance_ridge"))

• Return value through the ledger: fullseye.ledger.distance_ridge(...) returns only the declared out type voxel (the underlying function also returns auxiliary values). When you need what was dropped, use fullseye.ledger.distance_ridge.raw(...) or call medial.distance_ridge directly.

• Underlying return: (ridge, dist)

Usage

Extract the ridge of the EDT (the local maxima of the distance field) as the medial axis. Returns (ridge_mask, edt).

Computes the EDT of each foreground voxel and treats local maxima over the 26-neighbourhood (own EDT at least the maximum of the surrounding 26 voxels) as medial. This criterion naturally yields a dimension that follows the local dimensionality of the object:

blob (sphere) -> EDT unimodal -> point-like medial (1 centre point).

tube (cylinder)-> flat along the axis, unimodal radially -> line-like medial (axis line).

plate (slab)-> flat in-plane, unimodal across the thickness -> surface-like medial (mid-surface).

A boundary voxel always has a larger inner neighbour, so it is never a maximum and the outer shell drops out naturally. Flat ridges (axis/plane) remain as continuous lines/surfaces because equal-valued neighbours are allowed (>=).

Args:

vol: binary voxels (bool / 0-1 3D).

min_radius: threshold that discards weak ridges with EDT at or below this value (default 0 = discard none). For noise suppression.

Returns:

ridge_mask (bool 3D): medial voxels.

edt (float64 3D): Euclidean distance from each voxel to the background (= local radius).
